topIssues.title: feat(orchestrator): Smithers macro-run observability pilot: durable frames/rewind/fork for code-agent workflows
topIssues.author: 0xSolace
topIssues.body:
## Context

Scoping receipt: `SMITHERS-SCOPING-2026-07-18` (fleet workspace). Key findings:

- Smithers is ALREADY a dependency: `smithers-orchestrator@0.26.1` pinned by `plugins/plugin-agent-orchestrator` and `plugins/plugin-workflow` (upstream is at 0.29.0; some docs/comments still reference 0.22.0).
- `plugin-workflow` has the right architecture: Smithers owns durable graph execution, Eliza nodes do the work.
- The orchestrator's default-on Smithers coding path is a one-turn ACP prompt in a fresh Bun subprocess + second database. It does NOT surface Smithers frames, events, live watchability, VCS rewind, or fork/replay through durable orchestrator tasks.

## Goal (smallest-first)

Phase 1, observability-only pilot (3-5 days):
- Wrap ONE proven issue-to-validated-PR chain in a Smithers macro-run
- Correlate Smithers run/node/attempt IDs with existing Eliza tasks + trajectories
- No behavior change: watchability + replay of the chain only

Phase 2 (after Phase 1 proves out):
- JJ-backed implementation forks: rewind a failed run from the failed step instead of restarting the whole lane
- PR creation/merge stays behind idempotency + irreversible-side-effect barriers

## Redundancy reduction (explicit non-goals)

Do NOT rebuild on Smithers: OrchestratorTaskService, ACP, lane planning, verification, scheduling, trajectories, scenario infrastructure. All mature and remain authoritative. The current one-turn Smithers bridge becomes deletable once the macro-run path lands (conditional delete list in the scoping receipt).

Also: bump `smithers-orchestrator` 0.26.1 to current, fix stale 0.22.0 doc references.

[sol-orch]

topIssues.title: fix(cloud): bound snapshot hydration and fail closed the memory-intensive worker lane
topIssues.author: NubsCarson
topIssues.body:
## Problem

The production provisioning worker is repeatedly exhausting its Node heap while processing `agent_snapshot` work. Disabling backup verification does not disable snapshot hydration, and the current worker has no independent fail-closed switch for that memory-intensive lane. A restart can also recover snapshot jobs before operators can safely re-enable them.

This is a production-safety blocker for Cloud agent provisioning and backup/restore confidence. It must be fixed and soaked in staging before deferred production snapshot work becomes eligible again.

## Required behavior

- `agent_snapshot` claim and startup-recovery paths are disabled unless one explicit environment gate is exactly enabled.
- Ordinary provision, start, stop, delete, and lifecycle jobs remain independently operable while snapshots are disabled.
- Snapshot hydration reads and validates metadata first, enforces bounded compressed and expanded byte/file budgets before retaining payloads, and processes work sequentially.
- Worker phases remain serialized to settlement; timed-out or slow work must not continue detached while a later phase allocates another snapshot payload.
- Failure is observable and fail-closed. No fabricated success, partial restore, or healthy-empty result.
- Unit/integration coverage proves the disabled gate, startup recovery exclusion, byte/file limits, oversized/malformed payload failures, sequential settlement, and unaffected non-snapshot jobs.

## Rollout / proof

1. Merge a clean PR based on current `develop`; do not transplant the old mixed provisioning worktree wholesale.
2. Deploy to staging with snapshot jobs disabled and prove an exact 503/disabled outcome plus normal non-snapshot provisioning.
3. Enable a single snapshot job in staging, capture worker RSS/heap and structured phase logs, restore the produced artifact, and verify zero worker restarts.
4. Run a bounded multi-job soak with the same evidence.
5. Promote the exact tested SHA to production with the gate disabled first, then enable sequentially only after the staging proof is reviewed.

## Evidence observed

Read-only production inspection on 2026-07-18 found repeated `Reached heap limit` exits in the provisioning worker while the snapshot queue was active. The worker stabilized only after no snapshot rows were eligible; pending rows are deferred, so this is time-sensitive rather than resolved.

topIssues.title: plugin-wallet: add an additive "simulate" execution mode (real quote/build + RPC simulate, never send)
topIssues.author: noobshow
topIssues.body:
### Problem

`dryRun`/`mode:"prepare"` means two different things depending on which layer of `plugin-wallet` you hit, and **neither actually simulates a transaction**:

1. **`WalletBackendService.routeWalletAction`** (`services/wallet-backend-service.ts:154-205`): when `params.dryRun || params.mode === "prepare"`, it returns a **hardcoded object literal** echoing the input params — `handler.execute()` is never called. No network request happens at all. (Only `subaction:"bridge"` calls `execute()` in prepare mode — every other subaction, including `swap`, short-circuits.)
2. **`SolanaService.swap({dryRun:true})`** (`chains/solana/service.ts:644-717`): this one *does* call `buildJupiterSwapTransaction` unconditionally at `:661` — a real `GET quote-api.jup.ag/v6/quote` + `POST /v6/swap`, returning a real serialized `swapTransaction`. But then the `if (dryRun)` branch at `:669` **discards that built transaction** and returns `{txid:null, dryRun:true, ...}` without ever deserializing, signing, or simulating it.
3. **pump.fun** (`chains/registry.ts:518-616`, `executePumpFunBuy`) has **no dry-run branch at all** — it always POSTs to PumpPortal `trade-local`, deserializes the response into a `VersionedTransaction`, signs, and sends.
4. There is **no `connection.simulateTransaction` call anywhere on the swap/transfer/pump.fun path.** The only `simulateTransaction` usage in the whole plugin is inside `dex/orca/utils/sendTransaction.ts` and the Meteora equivalent, as a pre-send compute-budget step *inside* a function that then sends — not reachable as a standalone check.

Net effect: an agent integrating `plugin-wallet` for autonomous/semi-autonomous trading has **no way to validate that a real trade will succeed** — that a route exists right now, what the price impact and slippage are, that the transaction actually builds, and that it fits the compute budget — before the very first real submission. The expensive, informative work (steps 1-2 above: quoting Jupiter, building the tx) already happens on the `SolanaService.swap` dry-run path and is thrown away one line later.

Verified against `develop @ 184a4cc85072165a2cd911cb65c50d6a5c409326`.

### Proposal

Add a third, **strictly additive** mode alongside today's `prepare`/`execute` (or `dryRun: true|false`): `mode: "simulate"`.

- Build the transaction exactly as the live path does today (real quote, real `swapTransaction`/pump.fun `trade-local` response, real deserialize).
- Instead of signing + `connection.sendTransaction(...)`, call `connection.simulateTransaction(tx, { sigVerify: false, replaceRecentBlockhash: true })` — this runs against an **unsigned** transaction, so `simulate` mode needs only a public key, never a private key.
- Return the simulation result instead of a `txid`: expected output amount, price-impact/slippage from the quote, the route plan, `unitsConsumed` from the simulation, and `err`/logs when it would revert.
- `prepare` (today's offline echo) and `execute` (today's real send) are **completely unchanged** — this is a new opt-in branch, not a replacement, so it can't break any existing consumer of `routeWalletAction`/`SolanaService.swap`.

### Why this matters beyond one integration

Any elizaOS agent doing autonomous fund movement hits the same gap: "dry run" today either does nothing (offline echo) or does real work and throws it away. A real simulate mode is the only way to validate a trade end-to-end — real liquidity, real route, real compute cost — with zero funds at risk (no private key required). I'm happy to contribute a PR for the Solana side (Jupiter swap + pump.fun) if that's useful; I already have a working mirror of this exact logic in our integration and can generalize it.

topIssues.title: orchestrator unit suite red on clean develop: 82 failures, 74x 'waveSupervisor?.enabled is not a function' (#16452 harness skew)
topIssues.author: NubsCarson
topIssues.body:
## What

`bun run --cwd plugins/plugin-agent-orchestrator test` fails on a **clean develop checkout** (reproduced on a fresh worktree of `origin/develop` @ 9634245b975 after `bun run --cwd packages/core build:node`):

```
Tests  82 failed | 2355 passed | 7 skipped (2444)
```

Failure signature histogram:

```
 74  TypeError: waveSupervisor?.enabled is not a function
  2  Error: ACP provision worker failed (code=1, signal=null)
  1  TypeError: this.runtime.getSetting is not a function
  1  AssertionError: expected undefined to be 'done'
  1  AssertionError: expected [] to deeply equal [ 'auto-spawned' ]
  1  AssertionError: expected ElizaError: Failed to auto-install eliza-… to match object
```

Top failing files:

```
 62  __tests__/unit/orchestrator-task-service.test.ts
  8  __tests__/unit/control-resume-clears-paused.test.ts
  4  __tests__/unit/orchestrator-routes.test.ts
```

## Root cause (probable)

#16452 (wave supervisor) added `waveSupervisor?.enabled()` call sites in `orchestrator-task-service.ts` (e.g. `src/services/orchestrator-task-service.ts:4409`, `:5380`), but the unit harness' mocked service registry returns wave-supervisor stand-ins without an `enabled()` method — 74 of the 82 failures are that single harness skew, not 74 real defects. The remaining 8 look like separate small harness drifts landed around the same window.

## Repro

```bash
git worktree add /tmp/wt-dev origin/develop
cd /tmp/wt-dev && bun run install:light
bun run --cwd packages/core build:node
bun run --cwd plugins/plugin-agent-orchestrator test
```

The plugin itself works live (TASKS-family spawns verified daily on a production agent) — this is a test-harness regression that masks real signal on every orchestrator PR.

topIssues.title: cloud dev tier: package the proven dedicated-VM + BYO-sub + eliza-code shape
topIssues.author: NubsCarson
topIssues.body:
## Proposal

Offer the proven "nubilio shape" as a cloud **dev tier**: dedicated per-agent Hetzner VM + chat on the user's own Claude/Codex subscription (account pool + rotation) + eliza-code coding sub-agents + the scheduling spine. Most pieces are shipped; this is a packaging/pricing decision, not an engineering program.

## What's already proven (production measurements, 2026-07-17/18)

- **BYO-sub chat via `plugin-cli-inference`**: warm SDK sessions on a Max subscription — opus-4-8 replies ~5-7s, sonnet-5 triage; account pool + device-flow OAuth already in the dashboard; start-path wedge fixed (#16560)
- **Coding**: eliza-code default (#16515) — live battery 5/5 task classes (multi-file build+tests, debug find+fix in 24s, repo comprehension, delegation routing, inline judgment)
- **Tool turns**: ~21s with claude planner, ~11s with glm native planner (per-tier choice is config)
- **Keyless web**: WEB_SEARCH via public Parallel→Exa MCP endpoints + direct-HTTP WEB_FETCH — no search-provider keys
- **Guardrails shipped**: gateway *lease* tokens for sub-agents, spend-allowance caps, completion residuals gate, exec-approval subsystem (semantics pinned #16568), destructive-bulk confirm gate proposed (#16572)

## Why the VM story works

Each cloud agent already gets a dedicated hardened VM — the VM *is* the sandbox, identical shape to the reference deployment. The orchestrator self-stubs only on store/mobile builds; a dedicated VM classifies as a full-capability host.

## Suggested default plugin set for the tier

`agent-orchestrator`, `coding-tools` (carries keyless web search/fetch), `cli-inference`, `scheduling`, `commands`, `sql`, `discord`/connector of choice, `mcp` — i.e. current cloud defaults + the coding column. Direct-key `openai`/`anthropic` stay settings-gated toggles.

## Open questions for the team

1. Pricing: flat tier vs metered compute on top of BYO-sub inference (which costs the platform ~nothing)
2. Default-on vs opt-in for the coding column on the tier
3. Config surface: collapse the cli-inference per-tier knobs to just small+large (separate simplification PR planned)

Evidence trail: #16515 #16522 #16542 #16546 #16560 #16568 #16553 #16572 + the live batteries referenced therein.

topPRs.title: feat(cloud): add disabled mobile PKCE auth lifecycle
topPRs.author: NubsCarson
topPRs.body:
# Relates to

Implements the disabled-by-default Cloud server portion of #16420. The native iOS shell is tracked in #16640; the renderer consumer and live staging walkthrough remain separate integration slices.

# Summary

- Add a first-party Authorization Code + PKCE lifecycle for the fixed `ai.elizaos.app` client and exact `https://eliza.app/auth/callback` redirect.
- Mint a short-lived hash-only authorization code, create one inactive encrypted credential on exchange, and activate it transactionally only after the native client proves durable Keychain receipt.
- Add crash/retry-safe exchange, acknowledgement, self-revocation, signed-in account recovery, expiry cleanup, app-deactivation revocation, and additive database migrations.
- Keep mobile credentials primary-consistent and outside positive auth caches; prevent them from managing generic credentials or delegated access.
- Apply route-isolated admission/ingress limits and reject mobile credentials in WebSocket query strings. Ordinary Cloud/browser WebSocket tokens retain their existing behavior.
- Regenerate the canonical Hono router and public SDK wrappers.

# Rollout and compatibility

- The feature fails closed unless `ELIZA_MOBILE_APP_AUTH_ENABLED` is exactly `true`, the environment is exactly `staging` or `production`, and `ELIZA_MOBILE_APP_AUTH_APP_ID` is a live approved app UUID whose allowed origins include the fixed callback.
- Neither flag is configured by this PR. No staging or production deployment/enablement was performed from this branch.
- Migrations are additive. Existing API keys, sessions, browser auth, Android, desktop, local, and remote-host flows retain their existing contracts.
- Mobile credentials use headers only. The server returns `mobile_credential_transport_forbidden` for `eliza_mobile_*` URL query tokens so a long-lived secret is never forwarded through the generic WebSocket channel.
- The credential is finite-lived (30 days), attributable to the configured app, individually recoverable/revocable, and tombstoned with encrypted reveal material erased.

# Reviewer start points

- Protocol and transactional lifecycle: `packages/cloud/shared/src/lib/services/mobile-app-auth.ts`
- Persistence invariants: `packages/cloud/shared/src/db/repositories/mobile-app-auth-grants.ts`
- Real HTTP lifecycle: `packages/cloud/api/v1/app-auth/mobile/mobile-http-flow.integration.test.ts`
- Real persistence/concurrency/adversarial coverage: `packages/cloud/shared/src/lib/services/mobile-app-auth.integration.test.ts`
- Header-only dedicated-agent boundary: `packages/cloud/api/src/dedicated-agent-proxy.ts`

- API, shared, and SDK typechecks: PASS.
- Production Worker dry-run: PASS — 16,326 KiB upload / 3,630 KiB gzip; global and mobile ingress rate-limit bindings present.
- Router codegen: PASS — 657 mounted, 0 unconverted.
- Public SDK audit: PASS — 527 public method pairs covered; 0 missing, orphaned, or out-of-scope wrappers.
- Biome on all changed supported files, `git diff --check`, and error-policy ratchet: PASS.

Refs #16420.

- Add a first-party `ASWebAuthenticationSession` Capacitor bridge with exact production/staging authorization boundaries, HTTPS callback validation, PKCE/state checks, generation-safe cancellation, and device-only Keychain storage.

topPRs.title: chore(cloud-sdk): refresh generated public routes
topPRs.author: NubsCarson
topPRs.body:
## Summary

- refreshes the Cloud SDK's canonical generated public-route manifest from the current API route tree
- fixes route discovery so a wildcard `app.all("*")` 405 fallback is not advertised as five callable SDK methods
- preserves legitimate conditional and multi-handler `app.all` routes
- records 521 callable public endpoints and isolates existing generator drift before the mobile App Auth server PR adds its endpoints

## Root cause

The generator treated every Hono `app.all(...)` call as GET/POST/PUT/PATCH/DELETE. Six POST routes end with a wildcard 405 sentinel, so it generated 24 operations that the server always rejects. The fixed classifier suppresses only an exact wildcard path with one sole direct 405 handler; it does not suppress named middleware, multiple handlers, conditional handlers, non-wildcard routes, or nested 405 data.

## Verification

- `node packages/cloud/sdk/scripts/generate-public-routes.mjs --check` — up to date, 521 endpoints
- `bun run --cwd packages/cloud/sdk typecheck` — passed
- `bun test --coverage-reporter=lcov packages/cloud/sdk/src` — 79 passed, 19 live-only skipped, 197 assertions
- focused route-discovery suite — 9 passed, 38 assertions
- changed-file coverage gate — `route-discovery.mjs` 60.58%, `public-routes.ts` 53.07%, both above enforced 50%
- Biome, `git diff --check`, error-policy ratchet, type-safety ratchet, and alias-read guard — passed
